newsitem.title: USA: US bond mart stability may lure more corp issuers.
newsitem.headline: US bond mart stability may lure more corp issuers.

text.p: The recent improvement in the tone of U.S. fixed-income markets may trigger a pickup in new supply of U.S. corporate bonds over the coming weeks, market players said.

"The government market is not as sloppy and (high-grade) corporate spreads seem to have found a floor," said one investment grade syndicate official. "The tone is better so issuers may feel like they can get deals done."
Junk bond players also reported a more optimistic near-term outlook as prices began to improve this week after several weeks of losses.
The junk bond market finished this week with upbeat news that net cash flows into high-yield bond mutual funds turned positive for the first time in five weeks.
AMG Data Services reported on Friday $101 million in net cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds for the week ended April 16.
Analysts said if junk bond prices keep rising, much of the money that left the market in recent weeks may now come back.
This is because most of the redemptions in recent weeks have came from money managers who base their investment decisions on price momentum, they said.

In additional to a better technical market environment, corporate bond issuers will continue to be attracted to current interest rates that are still relatively low on a historical basis, market players said.
They said that issuers may want to lock in long-term financing now in order to avoid potentially higher rates in the future.
Syndicate sources said next week's calendar is already beginning to fill up with junk bond and high-grade deals.
L-3 Communications Corp's $200 million junk bond offering is expected to be one of the premier deals for next week.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to finance the spinoff of the high-tech communications units of Lockheed Martin into a separate company.
Following the spinoff, the company will be jointly owned by a Lehman Brothers Inc investment partnership, Lockheed Martin and certain former Lockheed Martin executives.
Lehman Brothers will underwrite the offering of 10-year senior subordinated notes, expected later in the week.
Comcast Cable Communications, a unit of Comcast Corp, is planning a $1 billion senior note offering for next week.
